messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: SEV2 - LB_TARGET_HEALTH failing (us-west-2). Affected service: api.redwood.com. 502s and TLS handshake failures reported by synthetic checks and customer errors. Pager: pagerduty

pagerduty: #page fired -> escalation policy: prod-api-oncall. Incident key: PD-INC-9882. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-INC-9882

alex_g: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs + target health now. ping me if you see anything obvious.

mira_ng: +1 oncall here. noticing increased TLS handshake timeouts in frontend logs. curious if the cert rotation landed last night on the LB.

sam_sre: seeing a spike in 502s and 524s from the edge -> origin path. Grafana: error-rate for api.redwood.com in us-west-2: 12% over last 10m. Latency up ~300ms p50->p95.

devops-ci: running quick target health check from CLI.

devops-ci: ```bash
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:12345:targetgroup/tg-api/abcdef
```

devops-ci: output snippet: ```
"TargetHealthDescriptions": [
  {"Target": {"Id": "i-0a1b2c3d"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "TLS connection failed"}},
  {"Target": {"Id": "i-0f9e8d7c"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "healthy"}}
]
```

alex_g: good, so not all targets are down. looks like a subset failing TLS. pulling openssl from a failing target now.

alex_g: ```bash
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.com:443 -servername api.redwood.com
```

alex_g: result for failing target (via proxy): ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
140736...: SSL routines:tls12_check_server_sig:certificate verify failed
depth=2 C = US, O = ExampleCA, CN = ExampleCA Root
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
```

mira_ng: that smells like incomplete chain or intermediate missing on LB or backend. we rotated certs last night for the domain (letsencrypt -> internal CA) per ticket INF-452. could be missing intermediate being served to some clients.

ops_incident_handler: checked Route53 and edge caches. No anomalous DNS records. TTL for api.redwood.com is 60s. But I do see some clients hitting a different edge (old certificate) per synthetic dig logs.

dns-bot: DNS query sample from probe-us-west-1:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> api.redwood.com @8.8.8.8
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.com. 60 IN A 52.12.34.56
;; AUTHORITY SECTION:
redwood.example.com. 172800 IN NS ns-1.example.net.
```

sam_sre: possibility: partial cert rollout + LB target group has mixed instance types or AMIs: some hosts have new cert chain, others still serve old cert. Health checks hitting TLS verifying endpoints might fail on those with old chain.

mira_ng: confirming rolling deploy of edge-proxy happened ~02:15 UTC and cert script ran against a subset (was supposed to be phased). maybe automation bug left half the fleet with incomplete chain.

alex_g: mitigation options: 1) force failover of traffic to healthy AZs/targets; 2) update LB health check to use HTTP on /_health temporarily (bypass TLS); 3) re-deploy cert chain to remaining hosts; 4) rollback cert change to previous cert if available. which is fastest?

devops-ci: fastest is to flip health check to HTTP path for the target group and let ALB mark the TLS-failing hosts healthy (if backend returns 200). but that masks TLS issue; customers using custom TLS may still see handshake failures.

mira_ng: re-deploy cert chain is low-risk and should fix handshake failures at source. I can start rolling certificate push to the remaining nodes now. needs ~5m per host and we have ~8 hosts to patch.

pagerduty: escalation -> on-call manager notified. Next escalation in 10m if not acknowledged.

alex_g: start redeploy now, mira. I'll open a temporary LB health-check patch if we see more customer impact while you roll.

mira_ng: rolling certs now. patch script: ```bash
for host in $(cat failing-hosts.txt); do scp certchain.pem $host:/etc/ssl; ssh $host 'sudo systemctl restart edge-proxy'; done
```

mira_ng: first host patched, restarted. checking target health...

devops-ci: after restart, target i-0a1b2c3d -> TargetHealth: healthy. TLS handshake successful.

alex_g: good. keep rolling. notify when 50% done so we can consider removing temporary mitigations.

sam_sre: error-rate dropping: 12% -> 4% after first two hosts patched. p95 latency improving. still some clients show TLS error (maybe cached route to old edge).

ops_incident_handler: for customers hitting old edge, DNS TTL is 60s but upstream caches may hold older records. we should consider invalidating CDN or issuing purge to speed propagation.

mira_ng: purge edge cache on cloudfront for api.redwood.com path / - started. expect propagation within ~2-3m.

dns-bot: cloudfront invalidation submitted: ID I2A3B4C5.

pagerduty: alert acknowledged and assigned to alex_g, mira_ng. No escalation.

alex_g: Patch complete on all failing hosts. AB test: all targets show healthy. running curl against a variety of edges:

alex_g: ```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.com/_health --resolve api.redwood.com:443:52.12.34.56
```

alex_g: curl shows HTTPS 200 and certificate chain includes intermediate CA. openssl verify passes.

sam_sre: metrics stabilized. error-rate back to baseline <0.5% in us-west-2. p95 latency back to normal.

ops_incident_handler: customer impact summary for postmortem: ~12% of traffic in us-west experienced TLS handshake/502s for ~12 minutes. No data loss. Affected customers: a subset using dedicated routing via us-west endpoints; broad public traffic saw transient failures until certs redeployed and CDN invalidation completed.

mira_ng: root cause: incomplete cert chain deployment during phased cert rollout automation; deployment script didn't include intermediate cert on some hosts.

alex_g: remediation actions recorded: 1) revert automation to block phased rollout until verification checks pass; 2) add CI check that validates full cert chain on each host post-deploy; 3) increase health-check verbosity to indicate TLS chain error reason; 4) run audit to find other services with similar phased rollout logic.

pagerduty: incident resolved marker queued. Please add runbook notes and postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident PD-INC-9882 -> RESOLVED by alex_g at ts 1770004598. Summary: TLS handshake failures caused by incomplete cert chain during phased rollout. Duration: 00:12:37.

alex_g: handing off to oncall-next for overnight monitoring. short summary: cert rollout partial, patched all hosts, CDN invalidation, metrics normal. Action items in ticket INF-9882.

oncall-next: taking handoff. I'll run automated checks every 10m for next 2 hours and escalate if errors reappear.

ops_incident_handler: logging completed. please add any missing notes to INF-9882 and add postmortem owners. thanks all :tada:

mira_ng: leaving a short note for postmortem: verify scripts include full chain, add canary verification step that tests SSL chain from external vantage points before allowing phased rollout to continue.

sam_sre: added follow-ups to postmortem: alert tweak to surface 'certificate verify failed' in healthcheck reason earlier.

alex_g: closing thread. great work everyone.
